title: What Does the Bible Say About the Rapture? 24 Verses
description: The passages behind the rapture: the Bible verses on being caught up to meet the Lord, the day nobody knows and the end-times views Christians hold.
keywords: what does the bible say about the rapture
is the rapture in the bible
where is the rapture in the bible
summary: The word rapture does not appear in the World English Bible or the King James Version (0 verses). It comes from the Latin rapiemur, the Vulgate's rendering of 'we will be caught up' in 1 Thessalonians 4:17, and 'caught up' appears in 5 verses of the World English Bible. The central passages are 1 Thessalonians 4:13-18 and 1 Corinthians 15:51-52, where believers who are alive are changed and taken to meet the Lord in the air. Christians disagree on the timing: before the tribulation, in the middle, at the end, or as one event with Christ's return. Jesus says no one knows the day or hour (Matthew 24:36). The verses below are the ones every view relies on.

faqs.q: Is the rapture in the Bible?
faqs.a: The word is not, but the idea rests on 1 Thessalonians 4:16-17, where believers who are alive are 'caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air', and on 1 Corinthians 15:51-52. Whether this is a separate event before the tribulation or part of Christ's single return is the disagreement.

faqs.q: Where does the word rapture come from?
faqs.a: From the Latin rapiemur in the Vulgate's 1 Thessalonians 4:17, which translates the Greek harpazo, 'to seize or snatch away'. English Bibles render it 'caught up'. The modern pre-tribulation teaching spread in the 1800s through John Nelson Darby and the Scofield Reference Bible.

faqs.q: Can anyone know when the rapture happens?
faqs.a: No. Jesus says that nobody knows the day or hour, not the angels or the Son, only the Father (Matthew 24:36), and that his coming will be like a thief in the night (1 Thessalonians 5:2). Verses that set a date are not supported by any passage.

faqs.q: What are the main rapture views?
faqs.a: Pre-tribulation (believers are taken before the tribulation), mid-tribulation, post-tribulation (believers are caught up and meet Christ as he returns), and views that see no separate event. Verses such as Revelation 3:10 and Matthew 24:29-31 are used on different sides.
